headline: Framework-Agnostic Testing Methodology for AI Agents Released
summary: Open-sourced methodology includes 61 benchmarks, 58 test blocks, and maps to the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications.
details: Testing AI agents goes beyond simple responses; it involves verifying tool routing, call chaining, failure recovery, prompt injection resistance, and adherence to cost/latency budgets. A new, open-sourced methodology addresses these critical aspects.

The framework-agnostic approach ensures applicability across various languages, runtimes, and toolsets. It features a comprehensive map of 61 benchmarks, including BFCL, GAIA, and SWE-bench, categorized by their measurement focus.

The methodology comprises 58 universal test blocks across seven tiers, each defined by a tool-agnostic capability and a concrete reference implementation. These blocks cover core functionalities and error recovery scenarios.

Security is a key focus, with the full OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications (ASI01–ASI10) mapped to six universal security test blocks. This integration aids in identifying and mitigating agent-specific vulnerabilities.

Evaluation techniques are detailed, addressing LLM-as-Judge biases, different pass metrics, trajectory vs. end-state evaluation, observability via OpenTelemetry GenAI, and automated red-teaming with tools like garak and PyRIT.

The methodology also aligns with major regulatory frameworks, including NIST AI RMF, MITRE ATLAS, the EU AI Act, and ISO/IEC 42001, providing a robust foundation for compliance and responsible AI development.
Users can adapt the methodology by replacing reference implementation fields with their agent's specific tool names and expected outputs. Blank templates are provided for ease of use.
A case study featuring PheronAgent, a macOS agent with over 50 tools, demonstrates the practical application of the methodology. The focus remains on the methodology itself as the core product.

headline_marked: YouTube Star AboFlah [[Plans Cartoon Series]] with Spacetoon
headline: YouTube Star AboFlah Plans Cartoon Series with Spacetoon
summary: The 50-million-subscriber creator is venturing into animation with 'Slayman,' set to launch by year-end or early next year.
details: Hassan Suleiman, known online as AboFlah, is expanding his brand with a new animated series titled 'Slayman.' The series is a collaboration with Spacetoon, a media company AboFlah grew up watching.
The cartoon is expected to debut on Spacetoon by the end of 2024 or early 2025. AboFlah aims to deliver a positive message to his young audience through entertaining storytelling.

AboFlah, who has amassed 50 million subscribers, sees the move into animation as a natural progression to engage his predominantly young fanbase. He also has a goal of reaching 100 million subscribers.

The creator, who co-founded 8Flamez to manage creators and build infrastructure for the creator economy, prefers the spontaneity of social media over traditional television. He believes social media allows creators to be more authentic and experiment with ideas freely.

AboFlah's career began with challenges, including initial disapproval from his father. However, his success, particularly his record-breaking charity livestream that raised $11 million for refugees, has earned him his father's pride and satisfaction.
